subtopics.name: Inserting Data (INSERT INTO)
subtopics.content: The INSERT INTO statement is used to insert new records in a table. You can either specify both the column names and the values, or just the values if you are inserting data for all columns.

subtopics.name: Inserting Multiple Rows
subtopics.content: You can insert multiple rows into a table with a single INSERT INTO statement by separating the sets of values with commas. This approach is much more efficient than running separate INSERT statements.

subtopics.name: Updating Data (UPDATE)
subtopics.content: The UPDATE statement is used to modify the existing records in a table. You should always use the WHERE clause with UPDATE to specify which record(s) should be updated, to prevent modifying all records by accident.

subtopics.name: Deleting Data (DELETE)
subtopics.content: The DELETE statement is used to delete existing records in a table. Similar to the UPDATE statement, it is critical to use a WHERE clause to specify which records should be removed.

subtopics.name: Handling NULL values in data
subtopics.content: A field with a NULL value is a field with no value, which is different from a zero or a blank space. You must use the IS NULL or IS NOT NULL operators to check for NULL values, rather than standard comparison operators.

subtopics.name: Transactions intro (basic idea while modifying data)
subtopics.content: A database transaction is a sequence of operations performed as a single logical unit of work. Transactions ensure data integrity during INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations, using COMMIT to save changes and ROLLBACK to undo them.
